subject: Customer request: fixed exit fee and termination triggers for SLA failures
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@kinetix.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Chen <laura.chen@kinetix.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 08:12:00 -0400
Subject: Request: fixed exit fee & termination triggers for SLA failures

Vanessa —

Thanks for the run-through on Friday. As Kinetix moves toward a production rollout we need contractual assurances that go beyond service credits. Our legal and procurement teams have asked for the following remedies to be included in the Master Services Agreement: 

- A fixed exit fee (flat cash payment) equal to 6 months of committed monthly recurring charges (MRC) if Redwood fails to meet the agreed availability target (>= 99.5%) for three consecutive calendar months.
- Immediate termination rights for material outages (P1s) that cause data loss or repeated month-on-month availability degradations, without waiting for cure periods.
- Liquidated damages capped at 12 months of MRC for catastrophic failures.

I know this is heavier than the standard credit-based remedies — Kinetix’s compliance team is worried about downstream revenue and regulatory exposure, and they want a clear cash remedy that is easy to budget for. I attached our draft SLA ask.

Before we loop legal, is Redwood open to a structure like the one above or do you have a preferred alternative? We’re trying to avoid protracted redlines but need something our CFO can sign off on.

—Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Platform, Kinetix Labs
Attachments: Kinetix_SLA_ask_20280618.pdf
From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@kinetix.ai>
Cc: Laura Chen <laura.chen@kinetix.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 09:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Request: fixed exit fee & termination triggers for SLA failures

Samir —

Appreciate the clear ask and the attachment. I’ve looped in Rishi (legal) and Marissa (Customer Success) so we can pull together an operationally realistic counterproposal quickly. We’ve handled similar requests with enterprise customers and typically land on a mix of extended credits, staged termination triggers, and a capped cash remedy in limited situations.

I’ll aim to get a draft back by EOD tomorrow and propose a short call to align next week.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales Director, Redwood Inference
From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 09:18:00 -04:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: fixed exit fee & termination triggers for SLA failures

Team —

Forwarding Kinetix's SLA ask (attached). High level: they want a flat cash exit fee (6x MRC) if availability <99.5% for three consecutive months, immediate termination for material P1s, and a liquidated damages cap of 12x MRC.

My read: their request is a high cash exposure for us and likely non-starter without strong gating. Suggested negotiation points:

- Prefer staged remedies: 1) automatic service credits for month 1; 2) fee-at-risk (small fixed sum) if repeat month within 90 days; 3) termination only after 3x missed months with a cure window.
- Always include a technical cure period (30 days) and an operational remediation plan before termination rights vest.
- Cap any cash exit to a modest multiple (2-6 months) but prefer credits + a one-time fixed exit amount rather than open-ended LDs.
- For material data-loss P1s we should preserve limited termination rights but require root-cause review and remediation steps / postmortem.

Rishi — can legal draft a counter that:
  * offers a capped cash exit equal to 3 months MRC (not 6),
  * requires three consecutive calendar months below 99.5% and a 30-day cure period before termination, and
  * includes a separate process for data-loss incidents (escalation + verification) where termination may be accelerated but still requires evidence.

Marissa — from CS: can we offer operational mitigations (dedicated pool during ramp, weekly health reports, increased telemetry/audit logs) to reduce their appetite for a large cash remedy?

Aditya — please confirm whether we can offer a one-time onboarding discount/credit in lieu of a higher flat exit fee.

I attached a short draft counter for legal to iterate.

Thanks —
Vanessa
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 11:07:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: fixed exit fee & termination triggers for SLA failures

Agree with Vanessa's approach. Draft counter (summary):

1) Remedies model: primary remedy = service credits calculated monthly (standard). Secondary remedy = a limited cash exit equal to 3 months MRC if: 
   - availability < 99.5% for three consecutive calendar months, and
   - Redwood fails to cure within a 30-day remediation period after written notice.

2) Material incidents involving data loss: allow expedited termination rights but require independent forensic confirmation (customer-provided or mutually agreed third party) and a short remediation/cure process where possible.

3) Liquidated damages: propose a mutual cap at 12 months MRC only for proven catastrophic breaches (data loss causing regulatory penalties); otherwise deny open-ended LDs.

4) Reporting & evidence: Redwood will provide audit logs and incident timelines for remedial review; agree to weekly operational sync during remediation windows.

5) Commercial sweeteners: offer a one-time onboarding credit equal to 1 month MRC or temporary dedicated capacity during the first 90 days to reduce incident probability.

I'll prepare Redwood_SLA_counter_v1.docx with legal language. We should not accept unilateral immediate termination without cure and evidence.

—Rishi
Chief Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@kinetix.ai>
Cc: Laura Chen <laura.chen@kinetix.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Jun 2028 10:15:00 -04:00
Subject: Redwood counterproposal to Kinetix SLA remedies request

Samir —

Thanks again for the transparency. Attached is a short counterproposal (Redwood_SLA_counter_v1.docx) that tries to balance Kinetix’s need for predictable cash remedies with a pragmatic operational approach we can live with. Summary: 

- Primary remedy remains monthly service credits for missed SLOs.
- Limited cash exit: Redwood will agree to a one-time flat exit payment capped at 3 months MRC if Redwood fails to meet >=99.5% availability for three consecutive calendar months and fails to remediate within a 30-day cure period following written notice.
- Material data-loss incidents: Kinetix may pursue expedited termination where independent verification shows a material data compromise; termination still requires a short review period and evidence.
- Liquidated damages: capped at 12 months MRC only in confirmed catastrophic cases involving regulatory penalties; otherwise we propose credits or capped cash exit.
- Operational commitments: temporary dedicated capacity during initial ramp (90 days), weekly health reports during remediation windows, and access to relevant audit logs for incident investigation.
- Commercial: one-time onboarding credit equal to 1 month MRC if Kinetix signs a 12-month committed term.

Proposed next step: short call with your procurement/legal to review legal language and agree redline priorities. We can send a redline-ready doc once we align on the commercial cap and termination gating.

If this direction works, I’ll ask Rishi to circulate the legal draft and Marissa to set up telemetry access for your ops team.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales Director, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_SLA_counter_v1.docx
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@kinetix.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Chen <laura.chen@kinetix.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2028 17:46:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Redwood counterproposal to Kinetix SLA remedies request

Vanessa / team —

Thanks. The counter is reasonable as a starting point — the 3-month cap and cure period are closer to what our CFO would accept than the 6-month flat ask. A few follow-ups from procurement/legal:

- They want to see the precise redline text for the expedited termination carve (data-loss P1s) and the definition of "catastrophic" for the LD cap.
- We need continuous access to incident timelines and audit logs (not just on request) for the first 180 days post-go-live. Can Marissa confirm we can set up a read-only telemetry view?

If you can send the legal redline and the telemetry instructions, we’ll have our counsel review and return comments within 3 business days. Otherwise, happy to jump on a call.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Samir
Head of Platform, Kinetix Labs
